title: Redistribute Characters to Make All Strings Equal
summary: Given an array of strings words, determine if it is possible to make all strings in the array identical by performing any number of operations.
statement: Given an array of strings words, determine if it is possible to make all strings in the array identical by performing any number of operations. In one operation, you can pick any two distinct indices i and j (where words[i] is a non-empty string) and move any character from words[i] to any position within words[j]. Return true if all strings can be made equal, and false otherwise.
constraints: There are 1 through 100 nonempty lowercase words of length at most 100.
An operation moves one chosen character between different words and may insert it anywhere.
Return whether all words can be made exactly equal.
hints: Moving characters preserves the total count of every letter.
Count all letters across all words.
Every letter count must be divisible by the number of final equal words.
Divisibility is necessary because equal words use equal counts, and sufficient because arbitrary moves can distribute each letter's quotient to every word.
editorial: Divisibility is necessary because equal words use equal counts, and sufficient because arbitrary moves can distribute each letter's quotient to every word.

tests.explanation: Each of a, b, and c appears three times, so every final word can contain one of each.
The single b cannot be divided equally between two final words.
